messages:
alice: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need a concrete compatibility/shim strategy for v1 -> v2 API changes. main goals: no downtime for hosted customers, minimal SDK churn, and clear telemetry for migration progress. thoughts?

brian: my 2¢: runtime routing shim in the control plane sounds easiest for hosted. we can detect v1 clients by header and route to a v1-compat adapter. gives one place to patch behavioral diffs.

carla: +1 for centralizing, but watch out for model-level state like KV cache/stream offsets. some v1 behavior depended on implicit truncation of context; adapter will need to emulate that or we risk silent regressions.

alice: good call, Carla. proposal: shim layers separated by concern: 1) surface-level request/response normalization (headers, fields) 2) behavioral emulation (kv/cache, truncation) 3) metrics/telemetry tagging. team owning the runtime implements 1 & 2 for hosted; SDK teams implement 1 for private/dedicated.

dave: timeline idea: 6 week window for shim + canary on 10% of traffic, then 4 week monitoring, then opt-in deprecation notice before turning off. we should keep full shim for >=6 months to give customers time.

erin: what telemetry do we need to know clients are still on v1 vs migrated? suggest tags: compat.version, shim.path, shim-emulation-level. push to telemetry pipeline and graph daily % of v1 calls.

alice: agreed. example header for detection: `X-Redwood-Client-Version: v1` and shim honors `X-Compat-Mode: emulate-truncation` if SDK requests it. Keep the default conservative.

carla: sample adapter snippet for truncation emulation:
```
if (request.context_len + new_tokens > max_len) {
  // emulate v1: drop earliest frames until fits
  trim_prefix_frames();
}
```
We also need unit tests asserting behavior with long contexts.

brian: for private/on-prem we can't rely on control plane routing. SDKs should include a lightweight adapter factory: `CompatAdapter.forVersion('v1')` that apps can opt into. we should publish adapters for Node/Python/Go.

alice: action items: 
- runtime: implement detection + normalization + truncation emulation (owner: eng-runtime)
- sdk: publish adapters + docs + migration helper scripts (owner: devex)
- telemetry: add compat.* tags & dashboard (owner: eng-platform)
- docs: deprecation policy + sample migration checklist (owner: product)

erin: can we include a small canary circuit in the routing policy so if emulation error rate > threshold we fallback to strict reject and notify? avoids silent bad outputs.

dave: yes — rollout plan: stage 0 local tests, stage 1 internal traffic, stage 2 10% external canary, stage 3 50%, stage 4 full, with rollback on error budget breach.

alice: one more UX detail: we should return a `x-compat-warning` response header for v1 clients that are hitting emulation so customers see the banner. e.g., `X-Compat-Warning: v1-emulated; migrate-by=2025-10-01`.

carla: +1, and add an endpoint `/compat/status` that returns supported versions for hosted so clients can poll. small JSON like { "supported": ["v2"], "deprecated": ["v1"] } — useful for auto-updaters.

brian: note: keep the adapter code tidy and avoid large switch statements per-version. design as a chain of small transformers so future v0/v0.5 oddities are easier to patch.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/compat-shim v1.0 -> staging (triggered by alice) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alice: thanks all — I'll draft the follow-up RFC with the proposed layers, timeline, and owners. posting it to docs today and cc-ing product for migration notice wording. :thumbsup:
